paragraphs.title: The War Against Og, King of Bashan

easy.question: Where did Og king of Bashan come out to fight Israel?
answers: Edrei
Heshbon
Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that Og came out to fight at Edrei.

easy.question: Who said to Moses, “Do not fear him”?
answers: Og
The Lord
Sihon
easy.explanation: The Lord told Moses not to fear Og.

easy.question: What did the Israelites do to Og and his people?
answers: Made a covenant with them
Fled from them
Defeated them and left no survivors
easy.explanation: The Israelites struck Og and all his people until none remained.

medium.question: Why was Moses not to fear Og?
answers: Because the Lord would deliver Og, his people, and his land into Israel’s hand
Because Og did not come to fight
Because Og was a weak king
medium.explanation: The Lord promised that Og and his whole kingdom would be handed over to Israel.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in these verses?
answers: Israel defeated Og, and then Og came to fight
Israel went toward Bashan, Og came out against them, and Israel defeated him
The Lord compared Og with Sihon, and Israel retreated
medium.explanation: Israel first went toward Bashan, Og came out to fight, and Israel then defeated him.

medium.question: In the phrase “until none was left to him remaining,” what does the phrase mean?
answers: A palace
A victory
A survivor or remnant
medium.explanation: The verse means that no survivor or remnant of Og’s people was left.

challenge.question: What does the comparison between Og and Sihon teach?
answers: Israel would defeat Og just as they had defeated Sihon
Og and Sihon were the same person
Sihon helped Og in the battle
challenge.explanation: The Lord told Moses to deal with Og as he had dealt with Sihon, reinforcing the promise of victory.

challenge.question: What is implied by the statement that the Lord gave Og, his people, and his land into Israel’s hand?
answers: Only Og’s army was defeated
The victory included the king, the people, and control of the land
Israel received only the capital city
challenge.explanation: The verse lists Og, his people, and his land, describing a complete victory over the kingdom.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Og did not come to battle alone?
answers: He was king of Bashan
The battle took place at Edrei
He came with all his people
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Og came out with all his people.

questions.question: What does the comparison between Og and Sihon teach?
answers: Israel would defeat Og just as they had defeated Sihon
Og and Sihon were the same person
Sihon helped Og in the battle
questions.explanation: The Lord told Moses to deal with Og as he had dealt with Sihon, reinforcing the promise of victory.

questions.question: What is implied by the statement that the Lord gave Og, his people, and his land into Israel’s hand?
answers: Only Og’s army was defeated
The victory included the king, the people, and control of the land
Israel received only the capital city
questions.explanation: The verse lists Og, his people, and his land, describing a complete victory over the kingdom.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Og did not come to battle alone?
answers: He was king of Bashan
The battle took place at Edrei
He came with all his people
questions.explanation: The verse says that Og came out with all his people.

paragraphs.title: The Conquest of the Cities of Bashan

easy.question: How many cities were captured in the whole region of Argob?
answers: Twenty cities
Sixty cities
One hundred cities
easy.explanation: The verse says that there were sixty cities in the region of Argob.

easy.question: What is said about the cities of Og’s kingdom?
answers: They were all captured
Only one city was captured
No city was captured
easy.explanation: The verse says that there was not a city that Israel did not take from them.

easy.question: What did the Israelites do with the livestock and the spoil of the cities?
answers: Left them in the cities
Returned them to Og
Took them as their own
easy.explanation: The verse says that Israel took the livestock and the spoil for themselves.

medium.question: What was distinctive about most of the cities that were captured?
answers: They were fortified cities with high walls
They had no inhabitants
They were small towns without houses
medium.explanation: The cities had high walls, gates, and bars, showing that they were strongly fortified.

medium.question: In the phrase “unwalled towns a great many,” what does “unwalled towns” mean?
answers: Royal cities
Towns without fortified walls
Cities built in the mountains
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts fortified cities with many towns that had no walls.

medium.question: What did Israel do after capturing Og’s cities, as they had done to Sihon?
answers: Built new walls around them
Gave them back to Og
Destroyed the people in them
medium.explanation: The people, women, and children of every city were completely destroyed.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “sixty cities” and “there was not a city which we took not from them”?
answers: The conquest covered the entire region
Only a small part of Og’s kingdom was conquered
The cities surrendered without a fight
challenge.explanation: The number of cities and the statement that every city was taken emphasize the conquest’s wide scope.

challenge.question: What was the difference between the fate of the people and that of the livestock and spoil?
answers: Both the people and the spoil remained in the cities
The people were destroyed, while the livestock and spoil were taken
The people were taken, while the livestock was destroyed
challenge.explanation: The people were destroyed, but the livestock and spoil were taken as property.

challenge.question: Why does the verse emphasize that the cities had “gates, and bars”?
answers: To show that they were fortified and strong
To explain that they were abandoned
To say that the gates were made of gold
challenge.explanation: Gates and bars, together with high walls, emphasize the cities’ defenses.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “sixty cities” and “there was not a city which we took not from them”?
answers: The conquest covered the entire region
Only a small part of Og’s kingdom was conquered
The cities surrendered without a fight
questions.explanation: The number of cities and the statement that every city was taken emphasize the conquest’s wide scope.

questions.question: What was the difference between the fate of the people and that of the livestock and spoil?
answers: Both the people and the spoil remained in the cities
The people were destroyed, while the livestock and spoil were taken
The people were taken, while the livestock was destroyed
questions.explanation: The people were destroyed, but the livestock and spoil were taken as property.

questions.question: Why does the verse emphasize that the cities had “gates, and bars”?
answers: To show that they were fortified and strong
To explain that they were abandoned
To say that the gates were made of gold
questions.explanation: Gates and bars, together with high walls, emphasize the cities’ defenses.

paragraphs.title: The Conquered Land and Og’s Bed

easy.question: From whom was the land taken?
answers: The two kings of the Amorites
The king of Egypt
The king of Edom
easy.explanation: The land was taken from the two Amorite kings.

easy.question: What name did the Sidonians give to Mount Hermon?
answers: Shenir
Sirion
Salchah
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Sidonians called Hermon Sirion.

easy.question: What were the dimensions of Og’s bedstead?
answers: Four cubits by four cubits
Nine cubits by nine cubits
Nine cubits long and four cubits wide
easy.explanation: The verse gives its length as nine cubits and its width as four cubits.

medium.question: Which area is described after the verse says that the land reached Mount Hermon?
answers: Gilead and Bashan
Egypt and the Negev
Judah and Galilee
medium.explanation: The next verse describes Gilead and Bashan, reaching to Salchah and Edrei.

medium.question: What does the phrase “the remnant of giants” mean in “Og ... remained of the remnant of giants”?
answers: The Amorite kings
The remaining descendants of the giants
The people of Sidon
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the remaining members of the group described as giants.

medium.question: Which detail in verse 11 emphasizes Og’s unusual size?
answers: That he was king of Bashan
That he was connected with the Amorites
The large dimensions of his iron bedstead
medium.explanation: The iron bedstead’s great size highlights Og’s extraordinary stature.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Hermon had two different names in verse 9?
answers: Different peoples gave the same mountain different names
The mountain moved from place to place
There were two mountains called Hermon
challenge.explanation: The Sidonians called it Sirion, while the Amorites called it Shenir; both names refer to the same mountain.

challenge.question: What does “on this side Jordan” mean in this passage?
answers: Inside the Jordan River
On the side of the Jordan being described
West of the Great Sea
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies the land on the relevant side of the Jordan.

challenge.question: What exactly does the verse say about Og in relation to the giants?
answers: He was the first of the giants
He was their only king ever
He was the only one left of the remnant of giants
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically says that only Og remained of the remnant of giants.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Hermon had two different names in verse 9?
answers: Different peoples gave the same mountain different names
The mountain moved from place to place
There were two mountains called Hermon
questions.explanation: The Sidonians called it Sirion, while the Amorites called it Shenir; both names refer to the same mountain.

questions.question: What does “on this side Jordan” mean in this passage?
answers: Inside the Jordan River
On the side of the Jordan being described
West of the Great Sea
questions.explanation: The phrase identifies the land on the relevant side of the Jordan.

questions.question: What exactly does the verse say about Og in relation to the giants?
answers: He was the first of the giants
He was their only king ever
He was the only one left of the remnant of giants
questions.explanation: The verse specifically says that only Og remained of the remnant of giants.

paragraphs.title: The Land Given to Reuben and Gad

easy.question: Which land is described in the verse?
answers: This land
The land of Egypt
The land of the Philistines
easy.explanation: The verse begins by referring to “this land.”

easy.question: To whom were half of Mount Gilead and its cities given?
answers: The tribe of Judah
The Reubenites and the Gadites
The tribe of Levi
easy.explanation: The verse says that they were given to the Reubenites and the Gadites.

easy.question: Where did the described territory begin?
answers: At Jerusalem
At Mount Sinai
At Aroer by the river Arnon
easy.explanation: The verse begins the description at Aroer by the river Arnon.

medium.question: What is described as happening at that time?
answers: Israel possessed the land, and part of it was given to Reuben and Gad
Israel left Egypt
Moses built the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The verse describes both possessing the land and giving part of it to Reuben and Gad.

medium.question: In “the land which we possessed,” what does “possessed” mean?
answers: We left the land
We received and held the land
We searched for the land
medium.explanation: In context, possessing the land means receiving it and holding it as an inheritance.

medium.question: What relationship between the two parts of the verse is correct?
answers: The cities were given before Israel possessed the land
Reuben alone received all the land
After possessing the land, part of it was given to Reuben and Gad
medium.explanation: The verse first speaks of possessing the land and then of giving part of it to the two tribes.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the verse naming Reuben and Gad specifically?
answers: They received an inheritance in the area described
They did not share in the inheritance
They were the twelve tribes
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that this territory was given to the Reubenites and Gadites.

challenge.question: What did the portion given to Reuben and Gad include?
answers: Only the river Arnon
Half of Mount Gilead and its cities
All the land of Israel
challenge.explanation: The verse names half of Mount Gilead and its cities.

challenge.question: What order of actions is implied by the verse?
answers: The cities were given first, and then the land was conquered
The tribes left the land and then possessed it
The land was possessed first, and then part of it was given to the tribes
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions possessing the land before describing its distribution.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the verse naming Reuben and Gad specifically?
answers: They received an inheritance in the area described
They did not share in the inheritance
They were the twelve tribes
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that this territory was given to the Reubenites and Gadites.

questions.question: What did the portion given to Reuben and Gad include?
answers: Only the river Arnon
Half of Mount Gilead and its cities
All the land of Israel
questions.explanation: The verse names half of Mount Gilead and its cities.

questions.question: What order of actions is implied by the verse?
answers: The cities were given first, and then the land was conquered
The tribes left the land and then possessed it
The land was possessed first, and then part of it was given to the tribes
questions.explanation: The verse mentions possessing the land before describing its distribution.

paragraphs.title: The Half-Tribe of Manasseh and Jair’s Villages

easy.question: To whom were the rest of Gilead and all Bashan given?
answers: The tribe of Judah
The half-tribe of Manasseh
The tribe of Reuben
easy.explanation: The rest of Gilead and all Bashan were given to half of Manasseh.

easy.question: Who received Gilead?
answers: Jair
Og
Machir
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And I gave Gilead unto Machir.”

easy.question: What were the places Jair named after himself called?
answers: The villages of Jair
The land of giants
The cities of Bashan
easy.explanation: Jair named the places after himself, calling them the villages of Jair.

medium.question: Why was the whole region of Argob in Bashan called the land of giants?
answers: Because it belonged to Reuben
Because that was the name of the region
Because Jair built villages there
medium.explanation: The verse says that the region was called the land of giants.

medium.question: In “all the region of Argob,” what does “region” mean?
answers: A long cord
A measuring tool
An area or territory
medium.explanation: The word refers to a geographical area or territory.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: Jair took the region of Argob and named it after himself, and Gilead was given to Machir
Machir received Bashan, and Og later named it after Jair
Jair received Gilead, and then Reuben received Bashan
medium.explanation: The passage first describes Jair’s territory and name, then says that Gilead was given to Machir.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Gilead being given to Machir, even though it was assigned to half of Manasseh?
answers: Machir was part of Manasseh
Machir was king of Bashan
Machir belonged to Judah
challenge.explanation: Machir belonged to the family of Manasseh, so this fits the allotment to half of Manasseh.

challenge.question: What does “unto the coasts of Geshuri and Maachathi” show about Jair’s territory?
answers: It had no boundaries
It extended to the borders of neighboring peoples or regions
It included only the city of Jair
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies the limits of the territory by naming neighboring borders.

challenge.question: What does “unto this day” mean regarding the name Jair gave the territory?
answers: The name remained known when the account was written
Jair was still alive then
The place was rebuilt every year
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the name remained in use up to that time.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Gilead being given to Machir, even though it was assigned to half of Manasseh?
answers: Machir was part of Manasseh
Machir was king of Bashan
Machir belonged to Judah
questions.explanation: Machir belonged to the family of Manasseh, so this fits the allotment to half of Manasseh.

questions.question: What does “unto the coasts of Geshuri and Maachathi” show about Jair’s territory?
answers: It had no boundaries
It extended to the borders of neighboring peoples or regions
It included only the city of Jair
questions.explanation: The phrase identifies the limits of the territory by naming neighboring borders.

questions.question: What does “unto this day” mean regarding the name Jair gave the territory?
answers: The name remained known when the account was written
Jair was still alive then
The place was rebuilt every year
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the name remained in use up to that time.

paragraphs.title: The Boundaries of the Inheritances East of the Jordan

easy.question: Which two tribes received an inheritance from Gilead?
answers: Reuben and Gad
Judah and Benjamin
Dan and Naphtali
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly names the Reubenites and the Gadites.

easy.question: Which river is mentioned as a boundary of Reuben and Gad’s inheritance?
answers: The Kidron
The Arnon
The Zin
easy.explanation: The verse names the river Arnon as a boundary.

easy.question: Which sea is mentioned in verse 17?
answers: The Red Sea
The Great Sea
The Salt Sea
easy.explanation: The verse calls the sea of the plain the Salt Sea.

medium.question: What was the boundary of the Ammonites according to the verse?
answers: The river Jabbok
The river Arnon
The Sea of Galilee
medium.explanation: The verse identifies the Jabbok as the border of the Ammonites.

medium.question: In “under Ashdothpisgah,” what does the phrase describe?
answers: Springs
Slopes or foothills
Fortified cities
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the slopes or lower areas beneath Pisgah.

medium.question: Which sequence correctly describes part of the boundary in verse 17?
answers: From the Great Sea to the Sea of Galilee
From the Salt Sea to the river Arnon
From Chinnereth to the sea of the plain, which is the Salt Sea
medium.explanation: The verse describes the boundary from Chinnereth to the sea of the plain, identified as the Salt Sea.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the verse mentioning both the Arnon and the Jabbok?
answers: The inheritance was marked by natural boundaries
The tribes received all the land of Canaan
The inheritance lay within one city
challenge.explanation: The rivers function as natural boundary markers for the territory.

challenge.question: What exact detail does verse 17 give about the sea of the plain?
answers: It was also called the Sea of Galilee
It was identified with the Salt Sea
It lay west of the Jordan
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “the sea of the plain, even the salt sea.”

challenge.question: What geographical meaning is conveyed by mentioning “Jordan, and the coast thereof”?
answers: The Jordan formed part of the boundary
The Jordan was a city in the inheritance
The Jordan was a mountain in the east
challenge.explanation: The Jordan and its surrounding border are included in the boundary description.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the verse mentioning both the Arnon and the Jabbok?
answers: The inheritance was marked by natural boundaries
The tribes received all the land of Canaan
The inheritance lay within one city
questions.explanation: The rivers function as natural boundary markers for the territory.

questions.question: What exact detail does verse 17 give about the sea of the plain?
answers: It was also called the Sea of Galilee
It was identified with the Salt Sea
It lay west of the Jordan
questions.explanation: The verse says, “the sea of the plain, even the salt sea.”

questions.question: What geographical meaning is conveyed by mentioning “Jordan, and the coast thereof”?
answers: The Jordan formed part of the boundary
The Jordan was a city in the inheritance
The Jordan was a mountain in the east
questions.explanation: The Jordan and its surrounding border are included in the boundary description.

paragraphs.title: The Armed Men Who Helped Their Brothers

easy.question: What did the Lord give Israel to possess?
answers: This land
Egypt
Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord gave Israel this land to possess.

easy.question: Who was commanded to pass before the Israelites?
answers: The women and children
The men fit for war
The shepherds alone
easy.explanation: The armed men were to pass before their fellow Israelites.

easy.question: Where were the women, children, and livestock to remain?
answers: In the wilderness
Beyond the Jordan
In the cities given to them
easy.explanation: They were to remain in the cities because they had much livestock.

medium.question: Why were the women, children, and livestock allowed to remain in the cities?
answers: Because Israel had much livestock
Because they did not want to enter the land
Because the cities were too far away
medium.explanation: Moses says that the Israelites had much livestock, so their families and animals would remain in the cities.

medium.question: In “ye shall pass over armed before your brethren,” what does “armed” mean?
answers: People staying behind
People going at the front as soldiers
People caring for livestock
medium.explanation: The context shows that the armed men would lead the way in battle.

medium.question: When could the Israelites return to their own inheritance?
answers: Immediately after crossing the Jordan
When their livestock increased
After their brothers received rest and possessed the land
medium.explanation: They could return only after the other Israelites had received the land and rest.

challenge.question: What division of responsibilities appears in these verses?
answers: The fighting men help conquer the land while the families remain in the cities
The families go to war while the men remain in the cities
Everyone remains in the cities until the war ends
challenge.explanation: The armed men go before the others, while the women, children, and livestock remain in the cities.

challenge.question: What does “as well as unto you” emphasize in verse 20?
answers: Only the first Israelites would receive an inheritance
The other Israelites would also receive the land given by the Lord
The women and children would receive a separate inheritance
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the remaining Israelites would also receive land and rest.

challenge.question: What was the condition for the tribes who already had an inheritance to return?
answers: Their livestock had to increase
They had to build new cities
Their brothers had to receive rest and possess the land beyond the Jordan
challenge.explanation: Their return depended on their brothers completing their inheritance and receiving rest.

questions.question: What division of responsibilities appears in these verses?
answers: The fighting men help conquer the land while the families remain in the cities
The families go to war while the men remain in the cities
Everyone remains in the cities until the war ends
questions.explanation: The armed men go before the others, while the women, children, and livestock remain in the cities.

questions.question: What does “as well as unto you” emphasize in verse 20?
answers: Only the first Israelites would receive an inheritance
The other Israelites would also receive the land given by the Lord
The women and children would receive a separate inheritance
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the remaining Israelites would also receive land and rest.

questions.question: What was the condition for the tribes who already had an inheritance to return?
answers: Their livestock had to increase
They had to build new cities
Their brothers had to receive rest and possess the land beyond the Jordan
questions.explanation: Their return depended on their brothers completing their inheritance and receiving rest.

paragraphs.title: Joshua Strengthened and Told Not to Fear

easy.question: Whom did Moses command in this passage?
answers: Joshua
The kings of the land
All the priests
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And I commanded Joshua.”

easy.question: What were the Israelites told not to fear?
answers: The wilderness
The kingdoms
The sea
easy.explanation: Moses told them not to fear the kingdoms.

easy.question: Who would fight for Israel?
answers: Joshua
The two kings
The Lord your God
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord would fight for Israel.

medium.question: What would Joshua learn from what he had seen happen to the two kings?
answers: The Lord would do the same to the kingdoms Israel would pass through
Israel must not pass through other lands
Joshua would have to fight alone
medium.explanation: Moses says that the Lord would deal with the future kingdoms as he had dealt with the two kings.

medium.question: In “whither thou passest,” what does “passest” mean?
answers: Rule
Return
Go through
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the kingdoms through which Israel would travel.

medium.question: Why should the Israelites not fear the kingdoms?
answers: The kingdoms were weak
Joshua had already conquered them all
The Lord would fight for them
medium.explanation: The verse gives the Lord’s fighting on their behalf as the reason not to fear.

challenge.question: What does “Thine eyes have seen” imply about Joshua?
answers: Joshua had personally witnessed the Lord’s actions
Joshua had heard about them only from others
Joshua did not yet know about them
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Joshua himself had seen what the Lord had done.

challenge.question: What can be understood from “thou passest” in verse 21 and “Ye shall not fear them” in verse 22?
answers: Joshua alone would pass through the land
Moses first addresses Joshua and then addresses all the people
The two verses are unrelated
challenge.explanation: Verse 21 addresses Joshua in the singular, while verse 22 addresses the people in the plural.

challenge.question: What role does the example of the two kings play in Moses’ words?
answers: Their defeat proves what the Lord will do in the future
The two kings will help Israel
It explains why Israel must not cross the Jordan
challenge.explanation: Their defeat serves as evidence that the Lord will act similarly against future kingdoms.

questions.question: What does “Thine eyes have seen” imply about Joshua?
answers: Joshua had personally witnessed the Lord’s actions
Joshua had heard about them only from others
Joshua did not yet know about them
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Joshua himself had seen what the Lord had done.

questions.question: What can be understood from “thou passest” in verse 21 and “Ye shall not fear them” in verse 22?
answers: Joshua alone would pass through the land
Moses first addresses Joshua and then addresses all the people
The two verses are unrelated
questions.explanation: Verse 21 addresses Joshua in the singular, while verse 22 addresses the people in the plural.

questions.question: What role does the example of the two kings play in Moses’ words?
answers: Their defeat proves what the Lord will do in the future
The two kings will help Israel
It explains why Israel must not cross the Jordan
questions.explanation: Their defeat serves as evidence that the Lord will act similarly against future kingdoms.

paragraphs.title: Moses Pleads to See the Land

easy.question: To whom did Moses plead at the beginning of the passage?
answers: The Lord
Pharaoh
Joshua
easy.explanation: Moses says that he besought the Lord.

easy.question: What did Moses ask to see?
answers: Egypt
The good land
The Red Sea
easy.explanation: Moses asked to cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan.

easy.question: What did the Lord command Moses to do from the top of Pisgah?
answers: Build an altar
Go down to the people
Look in every direction and see
easy.explanation: Moses was told to look west, north, south, and east and behold the land.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in this passage?
answers: Moses sees the land, then pleads, and then the Lord answers
Moses pleads, asks to see the land, and the Lord refuses to let him cross
The Lord commands Moses to cross, and Moses refuses
medium.explanation: Moses first pleads to cross and see the land, but the Lord tells him that he will not cross.

medium.question: In “Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter,” what does the phrase mean?
answers: You have more time
You must speak loudly
Enough; do not continue asking
medium.explanation: The Lord tells Moses that he must stop asking about the matter.

medium.question: Why does Moses mention the Lord’s greatness and mighty hand before making his request?
answers: To base his request on the great works he had already seen
To ask the Lord for a new war
To explain why he must return to Egypt
medium.explanation: Moses appeals to the Lord’s greatness and power as the basis for his request.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “for your sakes” in verse 26?
answers: The people had no connection with the matter
The reason was connected with or concerned the people
Moses was asking a favor for a foreign king
challenge.explanation: The phrase connects the Lord’s anger and refusal to hear Moses with the people.

challenge.question: What does the list of directions—west, north, south, and east—emphasize?
answers: Moses had to travel in all four directions
He would receive a broad view of the land from every side
He was forbidden to look at the land
challenge.explanation: The directions emphasize that Moses would see the land broadly, even though he would not enter it.

challenge.question: What is the central contrast between Moses’ request and the Lord’s answer?
answers: Moses asked to speak, and the Lord asked him to be silent
Moses asked to see the summit, and the Lord told him to leave it
Moses asked to cross the Jordan, and the Lord said he could see but not cross
challenge.explanation: Moses asked to cross over, but the Lord told him that he would see the land without crossing the Jordan.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “for your sakes” in verse 26?
answers: The people had no connection with the matter
The reason was connected with or concerned the people
Moses was asking a favor for a foreign king
questions.explanation: The phrase connects the Lord’s anger and refusal to hear Moses with the people.

questions.question: What does the list of directions—west, north, south, and east—emphasize?
answers: Moses had to travel in all four directions
He would receive a broad view of the land from every side
He was forbidden to look at the land
questions.explanation: The directions emphasize that Moses would see the land broadly, even though he would not enter it.

questions.question: What is the central contrast between Moses’ request and the Lord’s answer?
answers: Moses asked to speak, and the Lord asked him to be silent
Moses asked to see the summit, and the Lord told him to leave it
Moses asked to cross the Jordan, and the Lord said he could see but not cross
questions.explanation: Moses asked to cross over, but the Lord told him that he would see the land without crossing the Jordan.

easy.question: Whom did Moses command to be encouraged and strengthened?
answers: Joshua
The people
Bethpeor
easy.explanation: Moses was told to charge, encourage, and strengthen Joshua.

easy.question: What would Joshua do before the people?
answers: Sit in the valley
Go before the people
Build Bethpeor
easy.explanation: Joshua would go before the people and lead them.

easy.question: Where did the Israelites stay?
answers: On the mountain
In the wilderness
In the valley opposite Bethpeor
easy.explanation: The passage ends by saying that they stayed in the valley opposite Bethpeor.

medium.question: Why did Joshua need encouragement and strength?
answers: He would lead the people and give them the land as an inheritance
He had to build a new city
He had to remain in the valley
medium.explanation: Joshua needed strength because he would lead the people and cause them to inherit the land.

medium.question: In “he shall cause them to inherit the land,” what does “cause them to inherit” mean?
answers: Hide the land from them
Give them the land as an inheritance
Drive them out of the land
medium.explanation: The context shows that Joshua would lead the people into possession of the land.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in the passage?
answers: The people stay in the valley, Joshua is chosen, and then Moses commands him
Joshua gives the people the land, they reach the valley, and then he is strengthened
Moses commands Joshua to be strengthened, Joshua will lead the people, and meanwhile the people stay in the valley
medium.explanation: The passage first gives the command to Joshua, then describes his future task, and finally states where the people were staying.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “he shall go over before this people” about Joshua’s role?
answers: He will be the leader who guides the people
He will only watch from the side
He will remain behind and not move
challenge.explanation: Going before the people describes leadership at the front of the nation.

challenge.question: What major difference between Moses’ and Joshua’s roles appears in the passage?
answers: Moses will stay in the valley, while Joshua will build Bethpeor
Joshua will lead the people and give them the land
Moses will lead the people, while Joshua will only see the land
challenge.explanation: Joshua is assigned the future task of leading the people and giving them the land.

challenge.question: What does the transition to “So we abode in the valley over against Bethpeor” emphasize?
answers: The people had already finished conquering the land
The command had nothing to do with the people
The people were in a specific place at that time, while Joshua’s role concerned the future
challenge.explanation: The verse gives the people’s present location, while Joshua’s leadership describes his future task.
